Hi Sarah — adding a few technical notes to make the measurement definitions actionable. I'm Ben, SE on the account.

1) Token-to-token latency definition: we propose measuring inter-token gap using a sliding window of 1s and reporting the 95th percentile of per-token inter-arrival times across all streaming sessions in the reporting window. This filters out single-sample jitter but captures sustained stalls.

2) End-to-end request latency: for non-streaming requests we measure from initial HTTP request arrival at the ingress to the last byte emitted to the client (end-of-stream). For streaming sessions the request-level metric will be P95 time-to-first-token and also P95 of final token emission conditioned on sessions that completed within 60s. We can include separate metrics to avoid mixing streaming and non-streaming distributions.

3) Exclusions: planned maintenance windows (we'll provide a 48hr rolling calendar), region failover where traffic is routed across regions for availability, and customer-caused rate-limits (e.g., unexpectedly corrupted requests) will be excluded. We will not exclude transient infra-side GC events unless they exceed the agreed incident threshold (we should define that).

4) Remedies: for pilot we suggest service credits tied to P95 breaches measured weekly. For GA we can add escalation credits and engineering support commitments.

Lauren — attaching a short markdown summary I will drop into the shared doc. Happy to walk through specifics on Thu as proposed.

Regards,
